newsitem.title: UK: Britannia sells Co-op 110,000 bank accounts.
newsitem.headline: Britannia sells Co-op 110,000 bank accounts.

text.p: Britain's Co-operative Bank said on Monday it had bought a portfolio of 110,000 current accounts from the Britannia Building Society as of January 31.
In a statement the bank explained that it had been administering the accounts on the Britannia's behalf since the product's launch in 1991, so customers would experience an automatic changeover.
No financial details of the transaction were initially avaliable.
Dave Smith, spokesman for Co-operative Bank, said the accounts represented a 10 percent increase in its total account base, giving it about 1.1 million customers.
As a result, the bank would confirm its role as the country's largest telephone banking operator as it offers all its current account customers phone-based facilities.
Asked what the impact of the deal would be on its administrative base, Smith said, "We're expanding our telephone banking and this helps."
Later this week the bank will start the second phase of recruitment at its second national call centre in Stockport, near Manchester, and planned to hire 200 people, he added.
